Subject: Post-demo: Private VPC connectivity options & next steps

Hi Maya / Raj —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have everything captured: 

What we heard:
- Primary requirement: customer-managed Private VPC (no public internet egress) for inference traffic and model storage.
- Must support either AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering depending on network/infosec constraints; IP allowlist alone is not sufficient for their compliance team.
- Need clarity on whether Finova will require cross-account peering (transitive routing concerns) or a PrivateLink endpoint per account.
- Expected q1 traffic: steady state ~200 reqs/min with occasional bursts; estimated baseline latency target <150ms p50 for inference.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Finova to confirm preferred connectivity option (PrivateLink vs peering) and whether they require a dedicated AWS account for Redwood endpoints (Raj to confirm by EOD 2/20).
2) Redwood to provide a short networking checklist (IP ranges, required ports, DNS advice) and a sample diagram for both PrivateLink and VPC peering flows (attached).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical deep dive with your infra team; Sergio/Vivek available next week (please propose slots).
4) We’ll draft an initial SOW stub and security questionnaire entry for SOC2/data residency items once you confirm connectivity approach.

Attachments: finova-networking-checklist.pdf (draft), redwood-private-vpc-arch.png (two-diagram view: PrivateLink vs Peering).

If this matches your understanding, I’ll loop in Legal for an SOW timeline and get Serena on standby for early onboarding.

Thanks —
Rachel

Thanks Rachel — this is great, and matches our notes. Quick answers:
- Our security team prefers PrivateLink for production traffic because it avoids peering/topology complexity, but they are open to peering for a pilot if PrivateLink pricing ends up too high.
- We will need a PrivateLink endpoint in our account(s) with interface ENIs in three AZs.
- We require an IP allowlist on top of PrivateLink for the management/control-plane APIs (outbound egress from our infra to Redwood control plane must be restricted).
- I’ll confirm whether we’ll create a dedicated AWS account for Redwood endpoints by Friday 2/20 — Raj is syncing with infra.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Private VPC connectivity options & next steps

Looping in a couple of networking notes we should bring to the deep dive with Finova: 

- PrivateLink pros/cons:
  - Pros: no cross-account routing, simple firewall policies, recommended by many compliance teams.
  - Cons: requires an interface endpoint per region/AZ, ENI IP allocation considerations, and per-hour endpoint charges (we should prepare ballpark cost delta vs peering).
- VPC Peering pros/cons:
  - Pros: lower steady-state cost, works well if Finova can tolerate peering topology and routing table complexity.
  - Cons: transitive routing disallowed (so if they want multi-account, need TGW), and review of route table limits/propagation required.
- Control plane & management APIs: we can offer an allowlistable control plane IP block for Finova's egress policy, plus mutual TLS for API calls. Need to confirm whether their egress proxies inspect mTLS; if so we may recommend an outbound proxy-friendly cert configuration.
- DNS: for PrivateLink we can publish a private hosted zone with records that resolve to the interface endpoints — confirm they want us to manage the private zone or provide guidance for self-management.

I’ll draft a short slide (3 slides) to run through cost/ops tradeoffs and example CloudFormation snippets for both flows.

Sergio
